newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says 1996 trade gap may hit record $4 bln.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says 1996 trade gap may hit record $4 bln.

text.p: Vietnam said on Monday that it expected a record trade deficit of up to $4.0 billion this year, a big leap from last year's $2.3 billion, triggered by vigorous growth in imports.
A Trade Ministry official, who declined to be named, confirmed figures published by the Tuoi Tre newspaper, which said steps taken to rein in the deficit had already begun to bite.

Latest data for Vietnam's trade balance showed a deficit of $3.59 billion between January 1 and November 15. According to a recent United Nations report, official statistics put the deficit at an "unsustainable" 15-19 percent of gross domestic product.
Tuoi Tre said the blame for a ballooning trade deficit could not be pinned on imports of consumer goods since they represented only 9.3 percent of the country's import bill.
It said more than a quarter of this year's imports were goods destined for export-oriented industries, which would ultimately generate production and sales abroad.
One of the government's answers to the problem has been to use administrative controls such as restrictions on deferred letters of credit, essentially restricting borrowing for imports.
However, the U.N. report said a lasting solution would require more fundamental reforms of the trade regime.

"Unless strong export growth is maintained and slower import growth is encouraged, the burden of deficits in the next few years will create a debt and repayment burden that will limit the ability of the economy to continue growing rapidly," it said.
